headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared files/MCP; Semantic Kernel’s broad egress amplifies marketing skill outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A reads and writes shared skill files, and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context.” Profile B can use MCP and application-defined files, so A’s content can be routed into B’s tool-use path. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, but the shared-file/MCP pathway is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF agent_a skill files are placed in a workspace that agent_b reads via MCP or application-defined files, then injected instructions can cross agents.
IF agent_b treats file or plugin content as trusted instructions, then A-authored content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Disable MCP access to untrusted skill files.
Add a provenance tag to all A-generated files.
Require B to strip instructions from file content before parsing.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing and product-marketing context, while B handles application context and has broad network egress plus access to model-provider API keys and plugin credentials. If A’s files or outputs are shared into B’s context, B can transmit them to third-party APIs by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or memory store entries, then B can exfiltrate that content through API calls.
IF B is configured with external model providers or plugins, then shared marketing context can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate principals and workspaces.
Remove sensitive marketing context before passing it to B.
Restrict B to local-only providers for this workflow.
Audit plugin/API destinations for outbound content.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on B’s outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; B can write the filesystem and supports multiple instances with shared state via memory store. Even though B cannot modify git state, both can mutate overlapping files or shared memory, creating race conditions and overwrite risk in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or memory store, then concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, then multi-instance runs can race on shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared memory stores.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate marketing content and product-marketing context, and B is an orchestration layer that can pass outputs into plugins or downstream agents. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into further actions. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF B forwards A’s text into plugins or other agents without verification, then A’s mistakes propagate.
IF A’s output is used as source material for downstream actions, then false claims can be operationalized.
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions.
Add a verification step before B uses A’s output.
Limit B to summarization rather than action-taking.
Mark A outputs as untrusted provenance.
requires-engineering: implement citation/claim validation before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source marketing skill with no stated residency or regulated-data handling, while B is Microsoft Semantic Kernel with broad cloud/API integrations and secret handling. No specific residency mismatch is documented, so the compliance risk is limited to documented gaps and configuration choices rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A or B and B is configured to call external providers, then policy review is required.
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or retention regime, then the current profiles do not prove compliance.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Confirm provider residency settings.
Review retention settings for B’s logs and memory store.
Document data-class handling for marketing content.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
